answer: To prevent Sybil attacks in an agent economy surveying permafrost across arctic tundra and boreal timber, nodes verify peer locations using solar dispersion measured through a calibrated prism. Agents cross-check refracted sunlight spectra against orbital ephemeris data, forcing an attacker to deploy discrete optical hardware at separate physical coordinates per identity. However, overcast skies and blowing snow scatter direct sunlight, causing spurious authentication failures.
